a4: WPL batting styles explorer

a4 helps a Women’s Premier League (WPL) franchise analyst preparing for the player auction answer one question:

In a given season, which batters score quickly without wasting balls, and how do they compare with the rest of the league?

The package contains:

  • wpl_batters: season-level batting summaries for every WPL batter who faced at least 20 balls in a season (2022/23 to 2025/26);
  • batting_profile(): compares batters with the league median for a season and labels each batter’s scoring style (attacking, rotator, boundary-reliant or low tempo); and
  • run_app(): launches an interactive Shiny app built on the data and function.

Documentation website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-vnay0004/

Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-vnay0004")

Launch the app 

library(a4)
run_app()

Choose a season, optionally a team, and a minimum number of balls faced. Batters in the upper-left of the chart score more boundaries and face fewer dot balls than the league median.

Use the function directly 

library(a4)

batting_profile(wpl_batters, "2024/25", min_balls = 100) |>
  head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 17
#>   season  batting_team   batter innings  runs balls_faced dismissals fours sixes
#>   <chr>   <chr>          <chr>    <int> <int>       <int>      <int> <int> <int>
#> 1 2024/25 Mumbai Indians NR Sc…      10   523         343          8    84     4
#> 2 2024/25 Royal Challen… EA Pe…       8   372         250          4    40    11
#> 3 2024/25 Mumbai Indians HK Ma…      10   307         250         10    42     9
#> 4 2024/25 Delhi Capitals Shafa…       9   304         199          8    34    16
#> 5 2024/25 Mumbai Indians H Kaur      10   302         195          9    38    11
#> 6 2024/25 Delhi Capitals MM La…       9   276         232          8    45     1
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: dot_balls <int>, strike_rate <dbl>, dot_percent <dbl>,
#> #   boundary_percent <dbl>, average <dbl>, median_dot_percent <dbl>,
#> #   median_boundary_percent <dbl>, style <chr>

Data

Ball-by-ball data come from Cricsheet, accessed through the cricketdata R package, and are used under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY 1.0).

The script data-raw/wpl_batters.R downloads the ball-by-ball records and summarises them to one row per batter, team and season. See ?wpl_batters for a full description of every column.

Interpret with care: batting rates ignore batting position, match situation and opposition strength, and styles are defined relative to each season’s median.

Generative AI declaration

I used GENAI while preparing this assignment. Specifically, I used it to:

  • set up the package structure, licence and DESCRIPTION file;
  • draft the roxygen2 documentation, this README, the vignette (including the interpretation and limitations sections) and the pkgdown configuration;
  • diagnose errors, including an empty-repository push failure, a masked function in my workspace that caused filter() to resolve to stats::filter(), an app layout problem, and an incorrect Bioconductor link on the pkgdown site.

I ran and tested all code, checked the calculated figures against the package data, and confirmed that devtools::check() passes and the app works after installation from GitHub. I am responsible for all submitted work.
